reviews.text:
The high price is undeniable, and the veterinarian's examination techniques and diagnostic abilities are lacking.

My beloved cat passed away from lymphoma. It progressed incredibly quickly. If we had been able to take her to a higher-level animal medical center instead, she might have been able to receive treatment in time.
Although it was a last-minute request, they were very helpful and accommodating.

My cat became ill, so I took her in for an emergency checkup.

The staff were very helpful, and I believe they provided appropriate treatment. Appointments are only possible with a referral from your regular vet. The cost is certainly high (approximately 100,000 yen for a half-day examination), but given their emergency response and advanced treatment options, it's a limited choice.

There are four free parking spaces at OnePark (plus a few paid spaces).

I took some photos to guide you, as getting lost can be a bit of a hassle. Please use them as a reference.

My dog ​​seized an opportunity to bite and tear a garbage bag, and it seems a piece of plastic got stuck in his mouth, causing him to struggle violently and panic.

The first hospital we went to, N Hospital in Shibuya Ward, provided terrible service, so we cut our visit short and went to TRVA Nighttime Emergency Animal Medical Center, where they saved my beloved dog.

I am so grateful for their quick response.

At the first hospital we went to, N Hospital, even though we had called ahead for an emergency, we were made to wait for over 20 minutes despite my dog ​​struggling violently and moving his mouth violently. They showed no concern.

Even when we finally got to examine him, the doctor didn't open my dog's mouth and simply said, "There's nothing in his mouth," and coldly asked, "If you're worried, we can give him a sedative and do an ultrasound, what do you want to do?" It was a very unsettling and unpleasant experience.

My dog ​​was clearly in discomfort, making chewing noises, but the doctor insisted there was no plastic, that they couldn't see anything, and refused to even try to look properly.

I asked them to take a good look inside my dog's mouth, but they said they couldn't because the dog wouldn't let me touch its mouth without a sedative.

I instantly realized that this wasn't the right place, that my beloved dog might die, so I ended the examination and immediately called the TRVA Nighttime Emergency Animal Medical Center, explained the situation, and headed there right away.

As soon as I arrived on the second floor of the hospital, a nurse came over, checked on my dog, and discovered the plastic in its mouth.

[The doctor at N Hospital had insisted there was nothing in its mouth, but the nurse looked inside and found the plastic right away!]

She then took my dog ​​to the examination room, where the doctor treated it immediately.

I was called into the examination room almost immediately, and when the doctor told me that the plastic had been removed, I was so relieved I almost cried.

She also carefully explained and suggested further treatment options. Since the plastic was gone and my dog ​​was feeling better, we decided to monitor it and go home that night.

The doctor was a very kind and thorough female doctor.

The kind and gentle way the vet spoke eased my anxiety, and the thorough explanation was a great relief.

The nurses were very quick to respond, the reception staff were kind, and the payment process was fast.

I am truly grateful from the bottom of my heart.

Thank you so much for providing nighttime consultations and saving my pet's life.

Everyone at the hospital worked incredibly hard.

This is a very, very good hospital that you can rely on and feel safe in.

I would recommend it to others.

I will definitely use their services again in the future.

My small dog started coughing uncontrollably, so I took him to the vet in the middle of the night. I was so grateful they could see him when other hospitals were closed. They took X-rays and diagnosed him as having no problems, but he continued coughing on the way home, so I went back the next day to a veterinary hospital near my home.

There, they took X-rays at two different times—once he inhaled and once he exhaled—and confirmed that his trachea was collapsing. They diagnosed him with bronchomalacia and prescribed the necessary injections and medication. He will require ongoing treatment.

The bill came to around 25,000 yen, including the nighttime surcharge. The vet at the Suginami Animal Nighttime Emergency Medical Center was young and kind, but I was disappointed that they sent me home saying he was fine since they couldn't find the cause, even though I had brought him in because something was wrong.

I was referred to this clinic by my regular doctor. The examination was very thorough, and they explained the current situation and suggested possible treatments. I wanted to spend as much time as possible with my pet at home, so I requested home observation, but they told me to come immediately if my pet seemed unwell at night, which was such a relief that I almost cried. All the nurses were also very kind.

My cat became ill, and although she received an IV drip at our regular vet in the evening, her condition worsened during the night.

We took her to this hospital, which we were told about, and admitted her overnight, but by the next morning she needed an oxygen mask.

Determining that we couldn't treat her there, we took her to the advanced medical center in Kawasaki, which we were also told about.

We were told she might die during the examination, and we prepared ourselves for the worst, but thankfully she recovered somewhat by the evening, and we were able to bring her home.

The cause was identified at the advanced medical center, and our regular vet prescribed medication, but a few months later, she became ill again in the same way.

Since it was nighttime, we took her back to TRVA, but the next morning she crossed the rainbow bridge...

Thank you so much for your help the other day.

Early Saturday morning, my dog ​​vomited and seemed unusually unwell, so I took him to a nearby clinic. They diagnosed him with acute pancreatitis, and he was hospitalized from morning until evening (because the staff had to leave at night).

Two days later, when I went to pick him up, his condition had worsened significantly. His breathing was labored, and his eyes were vacant. I knew something was seriously wrong, so I immediately called this hospital, which the clinic had recommended. They asked me to come right away, so I rushed him there.

The veterinarian and nurses immediately put an oxygen mask on him after noticing the color of his lips and did their best. The subsequent examinations and the process leading up to the results were incredibly smooth. It was a critical situation, and I was extremely anxious, so I was truly grateful for their help.

The results revealed that in addition to acute pancreatitis, he also had aspiration pneumonia.

He was immediately placed in an oxygen chamber.

However, the doctor said the next day or two would be critical. I was told this, and it was incredibly difficult to leave, but I decided to entrust my dog ​​to the professionals and proceeded with the hospitalization procedures. The process was smooth, and I am grateful.

After returning home, I prayed that I wouldn't receive any calls about a sudden change in his condition. However, around 3 AM that day, I received a call saying he had stopped breathing, and I rushed back.

As part of the pre-hospitalization agreement, I had chosen not to use an artificial heart-lung machine. However, I was told that he had started breathing again after being given the machine, so I went there with a hopeful heart.

Upon arrival, I was immediately allowed into the treatment room, and seeing my beloved dog connected to the heart-lung machine was heartbreaking. Despite the situation, the doctors treated us with sincerity. Thanks to them switching to the heart-lung machine immediately, I was able to be with my dog ​​until the end.

I knew that he would die if the heart-lung machine was removed, but I couldn't bring myself to make him suffer any more. It was a selfish human desire not to cause him any more pain. My memories of that time are fragmented, but the doctors and staff did their utmost to help us.

After she passed away, they washed her body thoroughly, and my beloved dog looked peaceful. That was my only solace.

I'm truly glad I went to this hospital for emergency care.

Thank you so much for everything.

My beloved Sherry.

I will always, always love you.

Let's be family again in our next lives.

Have you crossed the Rainbow Bridge 🌈? Mommy is worried because you were so timid. Cross it without worry 😌 Mommy will always be by your side.

My dog ​​became ill in the middle of the night, and I was so worried that I took him to the emergency vet.

However, during the examination, they explained the tests and procedures before a thorough physical examination had even been performed, which honestly left me quite confused. Upon checking, I realized that a physical examination hadn't even been done at that point.

Furthermore, before a clear course of action was decided, my dog ​​was fitted with a cone and placed in a cage, and it was heartbreaking to see how frightened he was.

Ultimately, he received only the bare minimum of treatment, and we went home.

While there were no major problems in the end, considering the nighttime consultation fees, the time spent, and my dog's stress, I strongly regret not waiting until morning and going to our regular vet.

I went to the vet feeling anxious, but by the time we left, I was left with a great deal of regret.

My dog ​​became ill, and they came to see us early in the morning.

When I called, they listened to the situation very carefully, and during the actual examination, the doctor explained my dog's condition very clearly.

They also treated my previous dog very kindly in an emergency, so I felt confident entrusting my current dog to them as well.

Even if your pet becomes ill in the middle of the night, this is a very reassuring medical center.

The location is in Fukasawa, near Yoga, along National Route 246.

There are four dedicated parking spaces nearby (free), which was very helpful.

I've used their services multiple times. I'm truly grateful for their ability to see my pet outside of my regular vet's hours and for their 24-hour support during hospitalization. Their diagnosis, treatment plan, morning and evening handovers, and information sharing with my regular vet were all handled with care. While hospitalization is very expensive, it's priceless for a pet's life, and having 24-hour professional support, even late at night, early in the morning, and during hospitalization, is rare, so I think the price is reasonable. The parking lot is a little far away, but the availability of four spaces is appreciated.

The only drawback is that the clinic is on the second floor and there's no elevator. This was extremely difficult when my large dog's condition worsened or it lost consciousness. I strongly felt that it would be much better if the imaging equipment on the first floor were on the other side.

My beloved toy poodle suddenly became ill in the middle of the night. I called ahead and they examined her, and they performed emergency surgery, treatment, and dialysis, giving her the best and most advanced treatment available at the time. Unfortunately, she died after surgery due to a postoperative infection and kidney failure due to shock. I brought her home, and she passed away shortly after. After much thought and research, I've concluded that this clinic truly stayed with my dog ​​24 hours a day, trying everything they could to keep her alive, and they gave me hope until the very end. The cause was probably cancer, but just like with humans, if we don't have a system in place for early detection and treatment of cancer in dogs, by the time it's discovered, it's almost too late, and I think the problem is that it's up to the doctors here to do all the work. CT scans for dogs require stressful anesthesia, and the cost is high, making it a difficult procedure, yet the progression of cancer in dogs is more than five times faster than in humans. I strongly hope that veterinarians and society as a whole will discuss this issue and work towards improvement. This has become quite long, but I am truly grateful to the doctors here for everything they did for us.

We had a slight cough since we brought our 10-month-old female Shih Tzu home.

We had been getting medication from the vet, but the cough didn't go away...
However, her chest sounds were clear, and her lungs seemed fine.

That day, she was fine in the morning and ate her food, but when I tried to give her a snack at lunchtime, she unusually refused to eat and lay down, breathing very laboredly.
I was shocked and wanted to take her to the vet, but unfortunately, our regular vet was closed that day, so I rushed her here.

A young female doctor listened very carefully to my concerns, then performed tests and explained everything to me.

She said, "She's developing pneumonia, and it could get worse, so we'll keep her here today," and she was admitted to the hospital that day.

As expected, her test results worsened rapidly, and she seemed to be in distress, struggling to breathe. However, they monitored her 24 hours a day, and I visited her every day out of concern. Each time, they carefully explained her condition. My regular vet also told me, "This hospital has truly excellent respiratory specialists, so it would be better for him to stay here a little longer." He seemed to be in a critical condition for several days, but finally his blood count stabilized for a few days.

I felt very reassured knowing that they had such great facilities and provided 24-hour care. I wanted to do everything I could for him, so I allowed him to stay a little longer.

Thanks to their care, his condition stabilized, and he was successfully transferred back to our regular vet, where he is scheduled to be discharged soon.

I am truly grateful to the doctors and staff. I am filled with gratitude. It's certainly not cheap, but I think it's a hospital that's worth it.

It's reassuring to know that this hospital is open even at night or when our regular vet is closed.

We have three pets, so I think we will need their services again in the future.

Thank you so much for everything.

The doctor saved our dog. When I called to schedule an appointment, the nurse or staff member who answered the phone was so kind and gentle, and their words were so warm that they calmed us down when we were starting to panic.
Accurate treatment and explanations. Reasonable and reasonable treatment fees.

A night-time emergency room created by a local veterinary clinic.
My beloved cat had a seizure at night, so I sought care here, as it is affiliated with my family doctor.

Dr. Njima, who treated me, was sympathetic to my distraught owner, but calmly explained my cat's current condition. He then presented options that were easy to understand.

The treatment details were promptly passed on to the family doctor, so treatment there from the following day went smoothly.

My beloved cat passed away a few days later, but the whole family was able to say goodbye in a way that was satisfactory to the owner. Above all, the existence of an ER affiliated with my family doctor was a great relief for me as an owner. Thank you for your efforts.

My pet's regular doctor is Peco Harajuku, but since it's an affiliated hospital with TRVA, I went there after 10pm.
It's a rare animal hospital in Tokyo that offers night-time appointments.
They're open until 6am, covering the valuable nighttime hours.

My pet's claw suddenly broke in the middle of the night and the bleeding wouldn't stop, so I called them at the last minute and they treated me very courteously.
What's most reassuring is that affiliated hospitals share data such as treatment and diagnosis with my pet's regular doctor.
I provided first aid that day, and when I took him back to Peco Harajuku later, the details of the examination were shared, so I was able to communicate quickly and respond quickly, which I was very grateful for.

There is free parking available at the nearby Onepark, with space for four cars.
I received your help when my dog ​​suddenly developed pulmonary edema.

Two months after adopting a retired pug, I visited the clinic because he started breathing heavily and vomiting in the middle of the night. They were happy to answer emergency phone calls.

They also said they would arrange a taxi if requested.

The diagnosis was elongated soft palate, and he was hospitalized until morning. I told the night doctor that I was on a diet and had lost 1kg in two months, but it seems that information hadn't been passed on to them. When I went to pick him up, the morning doctor warned me that he was "too fat," which was a shock. (After all, it was the previous owner who put him up that much...)

The cause and progress of hospitalization are probably the top priority, but both my dog ​​and I had been working hard on our diets, so I'm only giving it one star for that reason.

However, it's reassuring to know there's a clinic nearby that offers night-time consultations like this.

[Added January 2026]
I later visited the clinic for gastroenteritis and foreign object ingestion.

It's always busy, so it's difficult to get through on the phone, and the waiting room is often full.
Looking at the families in the waiting room, it seemed that some had come from outside the 23 wards.

Even in such circumstances, they were able to examine and treat patients thoroughly, so it took about an hour from when they arrived at the hospital to when they paid.

Also, when a dog or cat in a critical condition arrived, a nurse politely called out to the waiting room, "We will now begin treating emergency patients. We apologize for keeping you waiting."

Even though many people had come to the hospital because they were worried about their pets, not a single person expressed any dissatisfaction, and that sight left a lasting impression on me.

Prior to treatment, multiple tests were performed without any explanation of the contents or costs of the tests or confirmation of consent. As a result, in addition to the catheterization procedure, the cost of tests totaled over 60,000 yen, some of which were questionable in terms of urinary ...

I visited at 2 AM because my dog ​​had accidentally ingested something, and they kindly and appropriately treated him. Everything turned out alright, and he was able to return home healthy. Thank you very much.

My regular vet had a partnership with this clinic, so I called once when my cat was having a seizure late at night.

She had end-stage kidney disease. She was having repeated, small seizures, and I was so worried that I called crying, but I received a terrible response from a female staff member. She was cold and said things like, "There's nothing we can do just because she's having seizures," "We're busy right now," and "What do you, the owner, want to do?" I declined the examination and hung up, wanting her to pass away peacefully at home.

My cat passed away the next morning.

Even now, the memory makes me sad. It was late at night on May 23rd, 2025.

My beloved dog is suspected of having a herniated disc. On the evening of the 10th, I took him to our regular vet for a steroid injection, but during the night his limbs became weak and his breathing became labored. I contacted this clinic, which I was given a referral form for at checkout, hoping for help, but I was shocked by the cold response from the woman on the phone. I cried after hanging up.

I was told that because he had been examined at another clinic during the day, it would be considered a secondary consultation, and they basically couldn't make a diagnosis without a referral from my regular vet. If surgery had been performed within 48 hours, the complications would have been minimal... I'm truly puzzled as to why everyone's reviews are so high.

I urgently called because my dog ​​might have swallowed something, and the receptionist (a nurse?) and the doctor were incredibly kind and helpful. They listened carefully to the details over the phone and explained everything clearly, which put my mind at ease.

They said it seemed okay to just monitor him, so I didn't need to take him to the vet, but they gave me detailed instructions on how to handle the situation going forward and what to watch out for as he progresses.

I was panicking because it was outside of my regular vet's hours, but I'm so glad I called this clinic.

Thank you very much.

Come to think of it, I've used their services twice but haven't written a review.

The first time was almost 10 years ago. My grandmother overfed our dog, causing it to vomit violently in the middle of the night. Panicked, I grabbed the dog, almost in tears, and rushed it to the vet in a taxi.

The taxi driver was kind, the vet was kind, and thankfully, after an IV drip in its neck, the dog was fine and we got home safely.

The second time was two years ago. My dog ​​had developed cardiogenic pulmonary edema, and I transferred him from my regular vet to this clinic for overnight care.

My regular vet wrote down the treatment progress for the handover, and the vet here also carefully monitored the dog's condition and managed the oxygen levels until morning.

When I went to pick up the dog, the door leading to the treatment room was left open while I was talking to the vet in the examination room. The vet saw the dog staring intently at me from the oxygen chamber in the treatment room and laughed, saying, "Ah, you noticed me! (laughs)." That was quite memorable. I remember feeling incredibly relieved when I saw that my dog's breathing, which had been labored from midday the day before until almost 8 PM when I dropped him off, had completely calmed down by morning.

From night until morning, they took X-rays and performed blood tests, apparently checking everything to prepare for any sudden changes in his condition. I also remember them telling me general information about dogs with this disease and condition, like what these numbers might indicate. They explained how we would manage his care going forward, including future plans.

Of course, it costs money because it's an emergency night clinic, but I think many animals have had their lives saved at this hospital.

I wish veterinary care were cheaper, but anyway, emergency night clinics are a lifeline for pet owners, so I hope this hospital continues to exist.

That being said, psychologically, it's a hospital I would never want to have to go to... (ToT) My heart aches every time I remember my dog ​​struggling to breathe. I hope veterinary care will continue to improve.

My regular vet had given me their business card in case of an emergency. I was out of town when my dog ​​suddenly had a seizure on its left front leg! It took about two hours to get back and have it examined. I was surprised by their courteous service and reasonable fees. Thankfully, it wasn't serious, which was a relief. I'm also grateful for the excellent service from the staff.

Despite telling them my cat is easily frightened, they were so rough with her that she was terrified the whole time, crying and screaming terribly.

They said they did a urine test, but the next day when I went to another hospital, they said they didn't even write down the results, which makes no sense.

I had to travel quite a distance to get her examined because there were no other places that would see her at night, but I will never use this hospital again.

Incidentally, I took her to another hospital the following day and the day after, and they held her gently, so she didn't struggle at all and didn't cry.
It was very helpful. I'm really grateful that I can get treatment at night.
Very good experience

My cat was lethargic due to diabetic ketoacidosis and was admitted to the hospital overnight.

The doctor in charge explained everything thoroughly, including the costs, and provided daily updates on her condition.

We are incredibly grateful for their unwavering support.

We had heard the costs would be high, so we transferred to our regular vet expecting a long treatment, but we were surprised that the actual cost wasn't that high.

Considering the level of care (attentive medical treatment, 24-hour nursing), the price was not only reasonable but even cheap.

We transferred after only four days because we were worried about the cost, but we really wished they could have continued treatment until she was more stable. Oh well, it couldn't be helped.

We are grateful to the doctor and nurses.

I received care at night.
My dog ​​chewed an Eve pill that was on the table at night, so I was worried and went to the hospital for treatment. The staff were very kind and easy to understand over the phone. I'm glad I've found a hospital I can go to again if something happens again.

My beloved cat was diagnosed with acute renal failure and required overnight consultations and half-day hospitalization. Thanks to Dr. S. Kimura's appropriate diagnosis and treatment, the emergency situation was resolved, and after he was discharged, he was admitted to a nearby veterinary hospital. He had repeated ureteral blockages, so we ended up performing a subsystem surgery, but he is now doing well and his kidney values ​​have returned to normal. I am extremely grateful to the doctor who initially responded calmly, and to everyone at the hospital. Thank you very much.

I was treated here overnight.
The reason for the low rating is that when I took my dog ​​home, the nurse (a petite woman in a reddish-purple uniform with inner colored hair) brought my exhausted dog from the treatment room with one hand. She brought my dog ​​in without supporting his bottom at all, with one hand dangling.
I've never seen anyone like that before.
If she treats dogs like this in public, how does she treat them behind the scenes?
Also, is this normal at this hospital?

The veterinarian who looked after me was a woman, and she performed a thorough examination and explanation, listening to my opinions as she went along.
Thank you very much.

Late at night, after being turned away by every other hospital, I finally got my cat examined here, which is quite far from my home. Ultimately, it was too late and my beloved cat couldn't be saved, but the vet explained her condition and the options for life-sustaining treatment very carefully, and the subsequent care was excellent. I wish there was a hospital like this closer to me.

My dog ​​had a polyp-like growth running from his throat to his trachea, which could potentially obstruct his breathing. This hospital was recommended by our regular vet because they specialized in respiratory issues. He was admitted for half a day under general anesthesia for various tests, costing over 200,000 yen for the hospitalization and tests alone. However, the cause wasn't clearly identified that day; they only explained that they wouldn't know for sure until they opened his throat for surgery. The surgery would cost 800,000 yen, so we tentatively scheduled the surgery and went home.

While I knew nothing was more important than my dog's health, I calmed down and decided to get a second opinion at another hospital specializing in respiratory issues. They determined the problem wasn't in the trachea, but in the palate, and there was no need for further hospitalization; they could perform surgery immediately. I immediately declined TRVA's services and opted for the new hospital. The surgery cost was covered by insurance, so my out-of-pocket expense was only 50,000-60,000 yen. After just one day in the hospital, my dog ​​was completely recovered and returned home.

So, what kind of hospital was this? They charged me 200,000 yen without even knowing the cause, just putting my dog ​​through unnecessary stress. They wouldn't even process the insurance claim, and when I tried to file a claim myself using the medical bill I received, I only got back about 1/20th of the money. I shudder to think what would have happened if they had gone ahead with that 800,000 yen surgery. I'll never go back to the hospital that recommended this one, claiming to be knowledgeable about respiratory issues, and I'll also never go back to this hospital, which acts like a monopoly, perhaps because they advertise themselves as a night-time clinic. Incidentally, I went during the daytime, so I don't understand why they charged me the night-time rate.

Please be careful, everyone.

I gave it one star because that was the lowest rating, but it doesn't even deserve a star. I know this is rude, but I'll say it: this hospital is full of incompetent people.
